text:
Emma (Product Designer): Quick design question — in the usage chart, should the cost axis show token-denominated labels (e.g. 1.2M tokens) or currency-denominated labels (e.g. $120)? Thinking about clarity for teams vs accounting.

Raj (PM): My gut: default to currency for the org-level view, tokens for project-level where devs care more about model units. But we need a clear switch/button.

Lina (Frontend Eng): Implementation note: switching labels is cheap, but the tricky part is aligning tick density across modes so charts don't reflow wildly on toggle.

Sam (Data Viz): Prefer tokens on short time windows (last 24h/7d) and currency for month/quarter. Tokens are noisy at short windows and useful for debugging.

Maya (Accessibility): If we add a toggle, ensure it's keyboard-focusable and has an aria-live region updating the selected unit. Also label the control clearly ("Show: $ / tokens").

Dave (Billing): From finance: users expect dollar values when exporting invoices or viewing billing rollups. If tokens are shown, show an estimated conversion rate somewhere (tokens -> $) and state that it's an estimate.

Emma: Good point, Dave. What about adding a small inline conversion row under the chart: "1.0M tokens ≈ $98 (est.)" — collapsible.

Raj: That sounds reasonable. UX question: where does the toggle live? Top-right of chart (inline) or global scope switch for org vs project?

Lina: Inline on the chart is easier for localized context. But we need persistence (per-user preference) — then we'd store it in the settings API.

Sam: Also recommend the axis label format use compact numbers and unit abbreviations: "1.2M tokens" / "$1.2k" — prevents clutter.

Maya: Ensure screen-reader text reads both value and unit, e.g., "one point two million tokens" vs "one thousand two hundred dollars". Use readableFull prop for sr-only copy.

Dave: On invoices: if a user drills from chart to invoice, keep the currency view by default on the invoice page. Tokens can still be exported as an alternate column.

Emma: Design mock pushed: https://figma.com/file/xyz (mock/frame: "usage-chart-token-toggle"). Key states: default currency (org view), token toggle collapsed, conversion row collapsed.

Raj: Can we add a small info tooltip "Why tokens?" that explains when to use tokens vs currency. Helps non-technical billing managers.

Lina: Will make the toggle accessible and add a preference endpoint. Need a copy of the conversion text for the tooltip.

Maya: Suggest tooltip copy: "Tokens show raw model units — useful for perf and quota troubleshooting. Currency shows billed cost." Short and scannable.

Sam: Chart technical: when switching units, animate ticks fade/slide rather than hard jump. Keeps context.

Emma: Ok design action items:
- Add inline token/$ toggle on chart (default behavior based on scope/time window)
- Add collapsible conversion row under chart
- Tooltip "Why tokens?" copy (Maya suggestion)
- Persist preference per user
- Accessible sr-only text and aria-live updates
- Smooth tick animation on switch (Sam)

Dave: One more billing edge: for accounts on committed plans, conversion must reflect committed discounts. Need to call billing API to compute displayed $ value.

Raj: Good catch — add note: conversion uses effective rate for the current account (discounts included). If rate unavailable, show "est." and a link to billing details.

Emma: I'll iterate mocks and update the Figma frame. Back after updates — tagging @Lina @Sam for implementation estimates.

ui-bot: Deploy preview for usage-chart branch is available at https://preview.redwood-inference.internal/usage-chart-2112 (staging)

Lina: I'll take a look at the preview tomorrow and estimate effort (likely 2-3 dev days + QA).
